safi-cedvel:1-10.t:
* I'rab:
(والنجم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم; (إذا) an adverb of future time, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to the omitted verb of the oath «[Note: There is a difficulty in this attachment: the verb of the oath is performative (inshāʾ), and the performative indicates the present, whereas the adverb (إذا) indicates the future, so there is a discrepancy between the two times ... To remove the difficulty the speech is construed as: I swear by the star at the time of its falling, whatever that time may be; the adverb on this view is borrowed for the present ...]» , (ما) negative in the three places; (عن الهوى) attached to (ينطق)..
The clause « (أقسم) بالنجم ... » has no grammatical position, being initial (ibtidāʾiyya); the clause «هوى ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «ما ضلّ صاحبكم ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath; the clause «ما غوى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the oath; and the clause «ما ينطق ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the oath. 4- 7- (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr), and the third-person pronoun in (علّمه) refers back to the Messenger, upon him be peace; (شديد) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. an angel severe in power; (ذو) a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هو), (الفاء) conjunction, and the fāʿil of (استوى) refers back, according to the apparent sense, to Jibrīl, upon him be peace «[Note: There are differing views on what the agent pronoun refers to: it was said that it refers to the Noble Quran, which settled in the breast of Jibrīl or in the breast of the Messenger, upon him be peace ... or it refers to the Messenger, i.e. he became upright in his strength or in his mission.. or it refers to Allah the Exalted, i.e. He established Himself on the Throne.]» , (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (هو) mubtadaʾ, i.e. Jibrīl; (بالأفق) khabar ...
The clause «إن هو إلّا وحي ... » has no grammatical position, being causal — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) —; the clause «يوحى ... » is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of وحي; the clause «علّمه شديد ... » is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of وحي, the link between them being implied (muqaddar), i.e. one severe in power taught it to him; the clause «استوى ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause علّمه; and the clause «هو بالأفق ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of استوى «[Note: On the assumption that the agent is Jibrīl; under the other construals of the agent the clause is resumptive.]» 8- 10- (ثمّ) a conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) in the two places, and the fāʿil of (دنا, تدلّى) is a pronoun referring back to Jibrīl, and likewise the noun of kāna; (قاب) the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb); (أو) a conjunction, and the fāʿil of the first (أوحى) is a pronoun referring back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, understood from the context of the verse in His saying عبده; (إلى عبده) attached to (أوحى), and the servant is Jibrīl, upon him be peace «[Note: It was said that it is the Prophet ﷺ, and the agent of both verbs in that case is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.]» , (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil of the second (أوحى) is a pronoun referring back to عبده, i.e. what Jibrīl revealed to the Prophet ﷺ.
The clause «دنا ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause استوى; the clause «تدلّى ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause دنا; the clause «كان قاب قوسين ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause تدلّى; the clause «أوحى (the first) » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of His saying, the Exalted: علّمه شديد القوى; and the clause «أوحى (the second) » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(6) مرّة: a noun meaning strength, vigour, soundness of mind, firmness ... etc.; its wazn is فِعلة, with kasra on the fāʾ, on the wazn of the maṣdar of manner. (8) دنا: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its imperfect is يدنو; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. (تدلّى), it contains iʿlāl by conversion; its origin is تدلّي — because the weak letter comes fifth, and its origin is wāw, from which is الدلو (the bucket) — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. (9) قاب: a noun meaning measure; of the bow, it is what is between the handle and its tip, and the bow has two qābs; its wazn is فعَل, with two fatḥas, and the alif in it is converted from wāw, its origin being قوب with two fatḥas; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. In the construction (قاب قوسين) there is an inversion (qalb), the origin being قابي قوس ...
(قوسين), dual of قوس, a concrete noun for the well-known instrument of war, or meaning the forearm's length; قوس is treated as masculine and feminine; its plural is قسي, its wazn فليّ with two kasras and a doubled yāʾ, and أقواس on the wazn أفعال, and قياس on the wazn فِعال with kasra on the fāʾ; it contains iʿlāl, its origin being قواس: when the qāf before the wāw took kasra, the wāw was converted to yāʾ. (10) أوحى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion; its origin is أوحي — with a yāʾ at its end — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Rhetoric:
The art of vagueness (fann al-ibhām): in His saying, the Exalted, فَأَوْحى إِلى عَبْدِهِ ما أَوْحى.
This is a magnification of the revelation that Allah revealed to him; the magnification is due to the vagueness in it, as though it were too great to be encompassed by any description. It is like His saying: (إِذْ يَغْشَى السِّدْرَةَ ما يَغْشى) and His saying (فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ ما غَشِيَهُمْ).

* Benefits:
- The Night Journey (al-Isrāʾ) and the Ascension (al-Miʿrāj)..
This was before the Hijra, and it was with his body and soul together. As for al-Isrāʾ, it is his travelling by night to Bayt al-Maqdis; as for al-Miʿrāj, it is his ascent to the highest heavens. This has come in the sound hadiths.
From Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was brought al-Burāq, an animal above a donkey and below a mule, which places its hoof at the furthest extent of its sight. I mounted it until I came to Bayt al-Maqdis, and tied it to the ring; then I entered the mosque and prayed two rakʿas in it; then I came out, and Jibrīl brought me a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Jibrīl said:
'You have chosen the fiṭra (the natural disposition).' Then we were taken up to the first heaven, up to the seventh." Jibrīl would ask for the gate to be opened at each heaven, and it would be said to him: Who are you? He would say: Jibrīl, and with me is Muhammad ﷺ. It would be asked: Has he been sent for? Jibrīl would say: Yes. And he ﷺ met a prophet in every heaven: in the first he met Ādam, in the second Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā, in the third Yūsuf, in the fourth Idrīs, in the fifth Hārūn, in the sixth Mūsā, and in the seventh Ibrāhīm, upon them be blessing and peace. "Then he took me to the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā), and behold, its leaves were like the ears of elephants and its fruits like large jars. When there covered it of the command of my Lord what covered it, it changed, so that none of Allah's creation is able to describe it for its beauty. Then Allah revealed to me what He revealed, and He made obligatory upon me and my community fifty prayers every day and night. I descended to Mūsā, and he said: Go back and ask your Lord for a reduction. I kept going back and forth between Mūsā and my Lord until my Lord, Glorified and Exalted, said: O Muhammad, they are five prayers, each prayer counting as ten, so that is fifty prayers. I descended to Mūsā, and he said: Go back and ask Him for a reduction. I said: I have become ashamed before my Lord." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from his journey and informed Quraysh; they called him a liar and asked him for descriptions of Bayt al-Maqdis, and his Lord displayed it for him, so he began describing it precisely. They asked him about a caravan of theirs, and he told them about it, and said: it will arrive on such-and-such a day, with the rising of the sun, led by a grey camel. On the appointed day, the disbelievers of Mecca went out to meet the caravan; one of them said: Here is the sun, it has risen; and another said: Here is the caravan, it has come, led by a grey camel. That only increased them in obstinacy and arrogance. Some people tried to shake the faith of Abū Bakr, and he said: By Allah, I would believe him in something greater than that.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative, and the second is relative: the fāʿil (agent) of (رأى) is a pronoun referring back to the Prophet ﷺ, and the returning pronoun is omitted, being a pronoun indicating the form of Jibrīl, upon him be peace «[Note: It was said that it is the Essence of Allah the Exalted, with disagreement among the views about these sayings between the hadiths narrated from ʿĀʾisha and those narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās.]» ...
The clause «ما كذب الفؤاد ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «رأى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the rebuking interrogative; (الفاء) conjunction; (على ما) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تمارونه) by making it include the meaning of تغلبونه (you contend to overcome him). The clause «تمارونه ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. do you deny his word and dispute with him; and the clause «يرى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:13-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (نزلة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being of the kind expressing number «[Note: Or it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. he saw him descending another time.]» , (عند) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رآه), (عندها) an adverb attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (جنّة). The clause «رآه ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «عندها جنّة ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from سدرة.]» 16- 18- (إذ) an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (رأى), (ما) a relative noun in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of the first (يغشى), and the fāʿil of the second (يغشى) is a pronoun, which is the one returning to ما; (ما) negative in the two places; (لقد رأى) like لقد رآه; (من آيات) attached to (رأى), and (من) is partitive «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from الكبرى, which is the object of رأى.]» .
The clause «يغشى السدرة ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «يغشى (the second) has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما); the clause «ما زاغ البصر ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of رآه.]» ; the clause «ما طغى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما زاغ البصر; and the clause «رأى ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(13) نزلة: a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar al-marra) from the triliteral (نزل); its wazn is فعْلة, with fatḥa then sukūn. (14) المنتهى: a noun of place from the five-letter verb انتهى; its wazn is مفتعَل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn; it may also be intended as the passive participle, i.e. the place to which one ends up.
(16) يغشى: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is يغشي — with yāʾ at its end — its past being غشي; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif and became يغشى. (17) زاغ: it contains iʿlāl by conversion; its origin is زيغ, its imperfect يزيغ; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Benefits:
- The nouns of time and place ...
They are two nouns indicating the time or place of the action ...
1- They are formed from the triliteral, when its ʿayn has fatḥa or ḍamma in the imperfect, on the wazn مفعَل, such as: شرب يشرب: مشرب. كتب يكتب: مكتب. Attached to this wazn is the triliteral with a weak final letter, such as: أوى يأوي: مأوى, as in the verse we are dealing with; سعى يسعى: مسعى; جرى يجري: مجرى.
2- They are formed from the triliteral, when its ʿayn has kasra in the imperfect, on the wazn (مفعِل), such as نزل ينزل: منزل. غزل يغزل: مغزل. Attached to this wazn is the triliteral with a weak first letter and a sound final letter, such as: وعد يعد: موعد. وقف يقف: موقف.
3- They are formed from what exceeds three letters on the wazn of its imperfect, after replacing the imperfect prefix with mīm and giving fatḥa to the letter before the last: ازدحم يزدحم: مزدحم. استعمل يستعمل:
مستعمل.
4- Whether the form is a noun of time or of place is distinguished from the context of the meaning. For example, if you say: منطلق الطائرة الساعة الخامسة مساء "The plane's departure is at five in the evening", then منطلق is a noun of time; but if you say مجتمع المسافرين في المحطة "The travellers' gathering place is in the station", then مجتمع is a noun of place. As for the form of the nouns of time and place from what exceeds three letters, it is like the form of the passive participle, and they are distinguished from the context of the meaning.

safi-cedvel:19-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the rebuking interrogative; (الفاء) conjunction, to make the seeing follow upon what was mentioned of the greatness of Allah the Exalted; (الأخرى) a second naʿt (adjective) of مناة, accusative (manṣūb). The clause «رأيتم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. have you known the greatness of Allah and His power, and then seen al-Lāt ... how contemptible it is and not worthy of worship «[Note: The second object of (رأيتم) is omitted, its implied form being: how powerless it is.. and some construed it with His saying, the Exalted:
أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثى
[.....]]»

* Morphology:
(اللات), the name of an idol, and (الألف) and (اللام) in it are redundant and obligatory, like those in الذي and التي. As for the (التاء), there is disagreement about it: it is radical according to some, from (لات يليت) meaning he withheld or diminished ... and it is augmentative according to others, so the word is from (لوى يلوى) because they used to turn (yalwūna) their necks towards it, or yaltawūna, i.e. they devoted themselves to it; the origin of the word is لوية, whose final radical (lām) was deleted, so the alif is converted from a wāw; this is the view taken by al-Muʿjam.. Some said that al-Lāt is taken from Allah. (العزّى), the name of an idol; it is فُعلى, with ḍamma then sukūn, from al-ʿizz (might), i.e. it is the feminine of الأعزّ; it was also said that it is the name of a tree that used to be worshipped. (مناة), the name of a rock that used to be worshipped besides Allah, derived from the verb منى يمني, i.e. he poured, because the blood of sacrificial animals used to be poured at it ... so its alif on this view is a yāʾ ...
al-ʿUkbarī says: «Its alif is from yāʾ, as in your saying مني يمني when he determined; and it may be from wāw, from which is منوان ... its wazn is فعَلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām. (الثالثة), feminine of الثالث, a noun for the ordering of number, on the wazn فاعل. «[Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of al-ʿUkbarī's quotation is missing in the source.]»

safi-cedvel:21-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the denying interrogative; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذكر), (له الأنثى) like لكم الذكر.
The clause «لكم الذكر ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «له الأنثى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one. 22- The reference in (تلك) is to the division understood from the interrogative; (إذا) a particle of response; (ضيزى) a naʿt (adjective) of قسمة, nominative (marfūʿ). The clause «تلك ... قسمة ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). 23- (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr), and (الواو) in (سمّيتموها) is redundant, a lengthening of the vowel of the mīm, and (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Note: I.e. you named the idols with them.]» (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, tawkīd (emphasis) for the fāʿil (agent) of سمّيتم; (آباؤكم) conjoined to the agent pronoun by the wāw, nominative; (ما) negative; (بها) attached to (أنزل) with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. for their worship; (سلطان) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi; (إن, إلّا) like the two previous ones; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to الظنّ by (الواو), the returning pronoun being omitted; (الواو) resumptive; (لقد جاءهم) like لقد رآه «[Note: In verse (13) of this sura.]» , (من ربّهم) attached to (جاءهم) «[Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الهدى.]» .
The clause «إن هي إلّا أسماء ... » has no grammatical position, being causal; the clause «سمّيتموها ... » is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of أسماء; the clause «ما أنزل اللَّه بها ... » is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of أسماء «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (سمّيتموها).]» ; the clause «إن يتّبعون إلّا الظن ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption; the clause «تهوى الأنفس ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما); and the clause «جاءهم ... الهدى» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ضيزى), meaning unjust. The word is either a derived adjective on the wazn فُعلى — with ḍamma on the fāʾ, then given kasra to suit the yāʾ — or a maṣdar like ذكرى used as a description. Its verb is ضاز يضيز in judgment, meaning he was unjust; and ضازه فيه يضوزه, meaning he diminished and defrauded him, of the pattern (bāb) ضرب ... al-ʿUkbarī said: «ضيزى: its origin is ضوزى, like طوبى; its first letter was given kasra, so the wāw was converted to yāʾ; it is not originally on فِعلى — with kasra on the fāʾ —» And in al-Qāmūs and Tāj al-ʿArūs it is both wāw-based and yāʾ-based, so there is no conversion in it.

* Rhetoric:
The art of rhymed prose (fann al-sajʿ): in His saying, the Exalted, «قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزى» .
There is a marvellous art in the word «ضيزى». The ignorant may wonder about the secret of using the word «ضيزى», which is uncouth and unfamiliar. In fact, the use of words has secrets, and this word which the Noble Quran used has a marvellous secret in its use: nothing else can fill its place. Do you not see that the whole sura, Sūrat al-Najm, is rhymed on the letter yāʾ? He the Exalted said: «وَالنَّجْمِ إِذا هَوى ما ضَلَّ صاحِبُكُمْ وَما غَوى», and so on to the end of the sura. When He mentioned the idols and the division of offspring, and what the disbelievers used to claim, He said: ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى تلك إذا قسمة ضيزى. So this word came on the rhyming letter on which the whole sura came, and nothing else can fill its place. And since the aim was to deride their saying, to carry out «[Translator's note: the text reads تنفيذ (carrying out), probably a misprint for تفنيد (refuting).]» their division, and to denounce it, a word suited to derision and denunciation was chosen for it, as though the baseness of the word pointed to the baseness of their understanding.
This is among the most wondrous instances in the Noble Quran of words matching the requirements of the situation.

safi-cedvel:24-25.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the hamza that is for denial; (للإنسان) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ما), the relative noun, the returning pronoun being omitted; (الفاء) causal; (اللَّه) «[Translator's note: so in the text; evidently (للَّه) is meant.]» attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الآخرة) ...
The clause «للإنسان ما تمنّى ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «تمنّى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما); and the clause «للَّه الآخرة ... » has no grammatical position, being causal.

* Morphology:
(تمنّى), it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is تمنّي; the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (كم) the declarative kam (khabariyya), meaning "many", in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (من ملك) the tamyīz (specification) of كم; (في السموات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of ملك; (لا) negative; (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is of the kind of the description, i.e. anything of availing; (إلّا) for exception; (من بعد) attached to a naʿt which is the implied (muqaddar) excepted, i.e. except an intercession after He permits; (أن) a maṣdar particle governing the accusative ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأذن) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (لمن) attached to (يأذن), and the fāʿil (agent) of (يشاء, يرضى) is a pronoun referring back to the Name of Majesty. The clause «كم من ملك ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «لا تغني شفاعتهم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (كم); the clause «يأذن اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن); the clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من); and the clause «يرضى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يشاء.

safi-cedvel:27-30.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative; (بالآخرة) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنون), (اللام) for emphasis; (تسمية) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: Or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they name the angels with the naming of the female.]» .
The clause «إنّ الذين لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); and the clause «يسمّون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna. 28- (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (ما) negative; (لهم) attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (به) attached to a ḥāl from علم; (علم) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (إن) negative; (إلا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (لا) negative; (من الحقّ) attached to (يغني) «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from (شيئا).]» by making it include the meaning of يفيد (benefits); (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being of the kind of the description, i.e. an availing neither little nor much ...
The clause «ما لهم به من علم ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; the clause «إن يتّبعون إلّا الظن ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); the clause «انّ الظن لا يغني ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and the clause «لا يغني من الحقّ ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna. 29- (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (عمّن) attached to (أعرض), (عن ذكرنا) attached to (تولّى), (إلّا) for restriction. The clause «أعرض ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if they follow conjecture, which is other than the truth, then turn away from them; the clause «تولّى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من); and the clause «لم يرد إلّا الحياة ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause. 30- The reference in (ذلك) is to seeking the world; (من العلم) attached to the khabar (مبلغهم); (هو) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, in the position of nominative, its khabar being (أعلم), (بمن) attached to (أعلم); (عن سبيله) attached to (ضلّ), (هو أعلم بمن اهتدى) like هو أعلم بمن ضلّ. The clause «ذلك مبلغهم ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical; the clause «إنّ ربّك ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of the command to turn away; the clause «هو أعلم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna; the clause «ضلّ ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative noun (من); the clause «هو أعلم (the second) » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause هو أعلم (the first); and the clause «اهتدى» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(27) يسمون: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by deletion: the final radical of the verb, the yāʾ, was deleted because it met, quiescent, with the wāw of the plural. (27) تسمية: a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb سمّى, and the tāʾ at its end is a substitute for the yāʾ of تفعيل, because yāʾ is the final radical of the word. (29) عن من: its writing in the Muṣḥaf came separated, while the analogy of the orthographic rule requires it to be joined (عمّن). (30) مبلغهم: a mīm-maṣdar from the triliteral بلغ; its wazn is مفعَل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn ... or it is a noun of place if what is intended by it is the degree reached in knowledge, knowledge being in degrees.
(اهتدى), the analogy of the iʿlāl in it is like (هدى) ... see verse (82) of Sūrat Ṭāhā.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (للَّه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) (ما), (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (ما في الأرض) conjoined to ما في السموات; (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (يجزي) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring back to the Name of Majesty; (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause is the ṣila.]» , the second (يجزي) is conjoined to the first, accusative; (بالحسنى) attached to the second (يجزي). The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجزي ... ) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being ملك «[Note: Or attached to (أعلم بمن ضلّ.. وبمن اهتدى), and the lām according to al-Zamakhsharī is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), not the lām of causation.]» , and the interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يجزي). The clause «للَّه ما في السموات ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «يجزي ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أنّ) «[Translator's note: so in the text; the implied particle is أن (an), as stated above.]» ; the clause «أساؤوا..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative noun (الذين); the clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما); the clause «يجزي (the second) » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يجزي (the first); and the clause «أحسنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) a relative noun in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) for الذين أحسنوا — in the previous verse — or as ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it..
or as the object of an implied verb أعني (I mean).]» , (الفواحش) conjoined to كبائر, accusative (manṣūb); (إلا) for exception; (اللمم) accusative as a disconnected exception (al-istithnāʾ al-munqaṭiʿ) «[Note: Some make al-lamam part of the major sins, so the exception is connected.]» , (بكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعلم); (إذ) an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (أعلم); (من الأرض) attached to (أنشأكم) with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. He produced your father; the second (إذ) is conjoined to the first; (في بطون) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (أجنّة), (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing; (بمن) attached to (أعلم) ...
The clause « (هم) الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); the clause «يجتنبون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «إنّ ربّك واسع ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of the exception of al-lamam; the clause «هو أعلم بكم ... » has no grammatical position, being another causal explanation; the clause «أنشأكم ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «أنتم أجنّة ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «لا تزكّوا ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if this is your state, then do not claim purity; the clause «هو أعلم ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of not claiming purity; and the clause «اتّقى» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(اللمم), a noun for minor sins; its origin is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the quadriliteral ألمّ بالمكان, i.e. his stay in it was short, and ألمّ بالشيء when he came near it without mixing with it; its wazn is فعَل, with two fatḥas. (أجنّة), plural of جنين, a noun for the child in its mother's womb; it is called janīn because of its being hidden in its mother's womb; its wazn is فعيل and the plural أفعلة, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

safi-cedvel:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation; (الفاء) resumptive; (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its description; (الهمزة) for denial; (عنده) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (علم), (الفاء) conjunction ...
The clause «رأيت ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «تولّى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي); the clause «أعطى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تولّى; the clause «أكدى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تولّى; the clause «عنده علم الغيب ... » is in the position of accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being رأيت in the sense of "inform me"; and the clause «هو يرى ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause عنده علم ...
And the clause «يرى ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).

* Morphology:
(أعطى), it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is أعطي with yāʾ; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. The origin of its final radical is wāw, for its triliteral is عطا يعطو عطوا الشيء, i.e. he took it. (أكدى), it contains iʿlāl by conversion like أعطى and on its analogy, but its final radical is yāʾ, for its triliteral is كديت أصابعه من الحفر, i.e. his fingers grew tired from digging ... then it was used for every quest that reaches nothing ...

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى.
He borrowed turning back and turning away for not entering into faith. This may be applied as a rule for the mention of al-tawallī in the Quran: wherever it occurs unrestricted and unqualified, its meaning is the absence of faith.
2- The explicit metaphor: in His saying, the Exalted, وَأَعْطى قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدى.
Here one who gives a little and then withholds from giving is likened to one who yukdī, i.e. who stops digging after being blocked by something hard like rock.

safi-cedvel:36-55.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the hamza that is for denial, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive verb is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, i.e. the one who turned away; (بما) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينبّأ), (في صحف) attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما) ...
The clause «لم ينبأ ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. 37- (الواو) conjunction; (إبراهيم) conjoined to موسى, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa; (الذي) a relative noun in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of إبراهيم; and the clause «وفّي ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي). 38- (ألّا) أن lightened from the heavy (anna), plus لا, negative; the noun of anna is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (وازرة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and it is a naʿt standing in for an omitted qualified noun, i.e. a burdened soul; (أخرى) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and it is a naʿt standing in for an omitted qualified noun, i.e. another soul ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تزر وازرة ... ) is in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) for the relative noun (ما) «[Note: It may be in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being ذلك or هو, and the clause is either an explication of (ما) or a ḥāl (circumstantial).]» ; and the clause «لا تزر وازرة ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the lightened أن. 39- (الواو) conjunction; (أن) like the first one; (للإنسان) attached to the khabar of laysa; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (ما) a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (ما سعى) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of laysa; the interpreted maṣdar (أن ليس للإنسان إلّا ما سعى) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the maṣdar ألّا تزر وازرة; and the clause «ليس للإنسان ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the second lightened (أن). 40- (الواو) conjunction; (سوف) a particle of the future, and the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive (يرى) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو, referring back to سعيه; the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ سعيه ... ) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تزر وازرة ... ); and the clause «سوف يرى ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna. 41- (ثمّ) a conjunction, and the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive (يجزاه) is a latent pronoun referring back to the human being, and the overt third-person pronoun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), referring back to the striving; (الجزاء) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) ...
The clause «يجزاه ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar of anna. 42- 43- (الواو) conjunction; (إلى ربّك) attached to the fronted khabar of anna; (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ ... «[Note: Or a pronoun borrowed for the position of accusative, as tawkīd (emphasis) for the pronoun that is the noun of anna ... or it is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) for emphasis.]»
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الى ربّك المنتهى) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar ألّا تزر وازرة; the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه هو أضحك) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar ألّا تزر وازرة; the clause «هو أضحك ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna; the clause «أضحك ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو); and the clause «أبكى ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أضحك. 44- 46- (الواو) conjunction; (أنّه هو أمات وأحيا) like (أنه هو أضحك وأبكى), in single words and clauses; (الواو) conjunction; (الذكر) a badal for الزوجين, accusative; (من نطفة) attached to (خلق), (إذا) an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to the implied (muqaddar) apodosis ...
The clause «خلق ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه خلق ... ) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar ألّا تزر وازرة ...
The clause «تمنى ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. when it is emitted, two mates are created ...
47- 51- (الواو) conjunction in the following places; (أنّ عليه النشأة) like أنّ إلى ربّك المنتهى, and the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ عليه النشأة) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar ألّا تزر وازرة..
(أنّه هو أغنى واقنى) like أنّه هو أضحك وأبكى, in single words and clauses ...
Likewise (أنّه هو ربّ ... ) and (أنّه أهلك ... ); (عادا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and by it He meant the tribe, so it was described by الأولى (feminine); likewise ثمود; (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) negative, and the object of (أبقى) is omitted, i.e. anyone of them ...
The clause «أبقى ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause that is the khabar of anna: (أهلك). 52- 53- (قوم) conjoined to (عادا), accusative; (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (أهلك), (هم) a separating pronoun for emphasis; (المؤتفكة) a fronted mafʿūl bihi, its governor being (أهوى) ...
The clause «إنّهم كانوا ... » has no grammatical position, being causal; the clause «كانوا ... أظلم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna; and the clause «أهوى ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أهلك. 54- (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. what He covered it with. The clause «غشّاها ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أهوى; and the clause «غشّى ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). 55- (الفاء) binding the apodosis of an implied condition; (بأي) attached to (تتمارى), the genitive word being an interrogative noun, and the agent pronoun in (تتمارى) refers back to the obstinate human being ...
The clause «تتمارى ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if Allah's power is embodied in what has been mentioned, then which of your Lord's favours will you dispute?

* Morphology:
(37) وفّي: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is وفي — with yāʾ — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif; its wazn is فعّل. (41) الأوفى: an elative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral وفى; its wazn is أفعل, with fatḥa on the hamza and the ʿayn; it contains conversion of the yāʾ to alif. (43) أبكى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being like that of (وفّي) ...
(46) تمنّى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being like that of وفّى; see verse (24) of this sura. (48) أقنى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being like that of (وفّى). (49) الشعرى: the name of a star in the sky — it was said they are two stars — as stated in Lisān al-ʿArab ... one of them is al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr — which is al-Shiʿrā al-Yamāniyya — and this one the tribe of Khuzāʿa used to worship, and al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumayṣāʾ, with ḍamma on the ghayn and fatḥa on the mīm. The wazn of الشعرى is الفِعلى, with kasra on the fāʾ. (51) أبقى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being like that of (وفّى). (52) أطغى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being like that of (وفّى), and it is an elative from the triliteral طغى; its wazn is أفعل. (53) أهوى: the word may be a verb or an elative, and the verbal reading is clearer ... it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being like (وفّى).
(54) غشي: it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being as in (وفّى). (55) تتمارى: it contains iʿlāl by conversion, its analogy being as in (وفّى).

* Rhetoric:
- Multiple antithesis (al-muqābala): in His saying, the Exalted, الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى.
Allah, Glorified be He, mentioned «أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكى», «أَماتَ وَأَحْيا» and «الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى»; the antithesis (al-ṭibāq) is multiplied, and for this reason it falls under the heading of muqābala. What has added beauty to this antithesis is that it came in the setting of eloquent rhymed prose, through the complete correspondence in the verse endings.

* Benefits:
- The pronoun called separating (faṣl) and support (ʿimād) ...
This pronoun occurs in many places in the verses of the Wise Book, and it occurs in the verse we are dealing with: (وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكى). The pronoun (هو) in the verse is called the pronoun of (separation, faṣl), because it separates between the khabar and a follower (tābiʿ), as in His saying, the Exalted: كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ, where the pronoun أنت separates between the noun of kunta and its khabar. And in view of the fact that this pronoun strengthens and emphasizes the speech, some of the Kufans called it (a prop, diʿāma), because the speech is propped up by it.
Its grammatical position: the Basrans held that it is a pronoun for emphasizing the speech, having no grammatical position, and the Kufans said: it has a position. Then al-Kisāʾī said: its position follows what comes after it, and al-Farrāʾ said: its position follows what comes before it. So its position between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar is nominative; between the two governed words of ẓanna it is accusative; between the two governed words of kāna it is nominative according to al-Farrāʾ and accusative according to al-Kisāʾī; and between the two governed words of inna, the reverse.
What constructions it admits: in His saying, the Exalted: كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ and إِنْ كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغالِبِينَ, the pronoun may be for separation or for emphasis, and it cannot validly be a mubtadaʾ, because what follows it is accusative.
In His saying, the Exalted: وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الصَّافُّونَ and our saying: (زيد هو العالم) and (إن زيدا هو الفاضل), the pronoun admits separation and being a mubtadaʾ, but not emphasis — because of the entry of the lām in the first, and because what precedes it is an overt noun in the second and third, since an overt noun is not emphasized by a pronoun, the pronoun being weak and the overt noun strong. It admits all three constructions in our saying: (أنت أنت الفاضل) and His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ.
As for His saying, the Exalted: أَنْ تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ, the pronoun هي is:
a mubtadaʾ, because what precedes it is an overt noun, so emphasis is ruled out, and indefinite, so separation is ruled out.

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(من النذر) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (نذير), and the reference is to the Noble Quran or to the Messenger, upon him be peace. The clause «هذا نذير ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(نذير), a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral أنذر, or it is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the verb if the reference is to the Noble Quran; and it is an adjective derived from the verb if the reference is to the Messenger, upon him be peace; its wazn is فعيل. (النذر), plural «[Translator's note: the text has جميع, evidently for جمع (plural).]» of نذير ... its wazn is فعُل, with two ḍammas.

safi-cedvel:57-58.t:
* I'rab:
(لها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of laysa; (من دون) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of (كاشفة), which is the postponed noun of laysa.
The clause «أزفت الآزفة ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «ليس لها ... كاشفة» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from الآزفة «[Note: Or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).]»

* Morphology:
(كاشفة), it may be a description, the feminine active participle of كاشف, or it may be a maṣdar like العافية; its wazn is فاعلة.

safi-cedvel:59-62.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the denying interrogative; (الفاء) resumptive; (من هذا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تعجبون)..
The clause «تعجبون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. 60- 61- (الواو) conjunction in the two places, and in the third it is of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (لا) negative ...
The clause «تضحكون ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تعجبون; the clause «لا تبكون ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تعجبون; and the clause «أنتم سامدون ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl «[Note: Or resumptive, with no grammatical position.]» 62- (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (للَّه) attached to (اسجدوا), (الواو) conjunction. The clause «اسجدوا ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you want deliverance from the punishment, then prostrate ...
And the clause «اعبدوا ... » is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.

* Morphology:
(تبكون), it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by making quiescent and iʿlāl by deletion ... its origin is تبكيون — with a yāʾ bearing ḍamma before the wāw — the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the kāf — iʿlāl by making quiescent — two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ and the wāw, so the yāʾ, the final radical of the word, was deleted, and it became تبكون, its wazn تفعون — iʿlāl by deletion. (سامدون), plural of سامد, an active participle from the triliteral (سمد), meaning he was heedless, of the pattern (bāb) نصر. al-Sumūd: it was said it is turning away, it was said it is amusement, it was said it is torpor, and it was said it is arrogance ...
